requirements.title: The company fulfills the eligibility requirements for B Corp Certification.

subRequirements.title: The company meets the necessary qualifications to pursue B Corp Certification.

criteria.text:
The company is confrmed to be:
a) an incorporated business entity
b) in operation for at least 12 months
c) generating a majority of revenue from a competitive market.

The company does not fall into any of the following categories.
a) Business divisions, brands, or units, or businesses that are not complete and distinct from their parent or group of affliates
b) Franchisors who do not own a majority of global franchisee locations, or franchisors without geographic distinction from independentfranchisees
c) Non-profts or Civil Society Organizations (CSOs), foundations, or charitable entities, unless otherwise approved by B Lab
d) Governments, government agencies, government ministries, or state-owned enterprises, unless otherwise approved by B Lab
e) Company legally registered in regions not covered operationally by B Lab and not part of a larger group registered in a region covered byB Lab

subRequirements.title: The company is not significantly involved in industries that undermine the B Lab Theory of Change

criteria.text:
The company generates less than 1% of annual revenue from causing or contributing to the impacts on affected stakeholders of the listedindustries:
a) Fossil fuel producers
b) Gambling
c) Pornography
d) Prisons and detention centers (including prison or detention center labor)
e) Tobacco
f) Weapons
If a company generates more than 1% of annual revenue from being linked to impacts on affected stakeholders in the listed industries,then they publicly report this.
For electric utilities and power generation companies, less than 50% of their product portfolio or energy mix is from fossil fuels.
B Corps certifed against version 6 of the standards must meet FR1.2 by Year 3 (not Year 0).

subRequirements.title: The company complies with local and national laws and regulations.

criteria.text: The company complies with all applicable local and national laws and regulations.
The company signs an Agreement committing to the B Corp Certifcation process.

subRequirements.title: The company shares accurate and complete information with B Lab.

criteria.text:
The company shares accurate and complete information by:
a) using credible evidence and data source
b) having a clear understanding of B Lab’s resources.

The company shares accurate and complete information at all times:
a) in its B Impact Assessment
b) in providing information to assurance providers authorized by B Lab
c) in all communications with B Lab personnel.
The company signs an Agreement committing to the B Corp Certifcation process.

subRequirements.title: The company is transparent about its performance against the B Lab Standard.

criteria.text: The company shares basic details for its B Corp public profle through the B Impact Assessment platform.
The company agrees to publicly share information as required by the B Lab Standard.
If the company is a wholly-owned or majority-owned subsidiary, or a large public company, it makes its entire B Impact Assessment reportpublic and identifes any majority owners.

The company agrees that B Lab can make its B Impact Report and basic profle information available on the B Lab Global website andother B Lab and Sistema B Global Partner websites while the company is a certifed B Corp
The company signs an Agreement committing to the B Corp Certifcation process.

requirements.title: The company adopts the B Corp legal requirement and commits to support the B Corp community’s collective purpose.

subRequirements.title: The company adopts the B Corp legal requirement in its corporate structure or governing documents.

criteria.text: The company adopts an entity type or an amendment to its governing documents to require stakeholder governance (meaning it considersstakeholders in its decision-making). The company adopts stakeholder governance in accordance with the B Corp legal requirement, and asapplicable to its legal form and jurisdiction.

If the company cannot adopt a stakeholder governance legal form because of local laws, it signs the B Corp Agreement and commits to:
a) working with B Lab to determine the appropriate legal pathway
b) advocating for beneft corporation legislation in its jurisdiction
c) amending its formation documents or adopting a new legal form if one is enacted through local lawmaking.
The company signs an Agreement committing to the B Corp Certifcation process.

subRequirements.title: The company signs the Declaration of Interdependence and commits to the shared collective purpose of the B Corp community

criteria.text: The company commits to the shared collective purpose of the B Corp community, as set out in the Declaration of Interdependence:We envision a global economy that uses business as a force for good. This economy is comprised of a new type of corporation — the BCorporation — which is purpose-driven and creates beneft for all stakeholders, not just shareholders.As Certifed B Corporations and leaders of this emerging economy, we believe:That we must be the change we seek in the world.That all business ought to be conducted as if people and place mattered.That, through their products, practices, and profts, businesses should aspire to do no harm and beneft all.To do so requires that we act with the understanding that we are each dependent upon another and thus responsible for each other and futuregenerations.
The company signs an Agreement committing to the B Corp Certifcation process.

requirements.title: The company creates a risk profile and meets any additional sub-requirements

subRequirements.title: The company creates a risk profile and meets any additional sub-requirements

criteria.text: TThe company creates a risk profle using B Lab’s Risk Tool by answering the 14 questions in FR3.1.a to FR3.1.n.
The company meets any additional Impact Topic sub-requirements that the Risk Tool activates.
The company agrees to a summary of the risk profle being displayed on its B Corp public profle

[Small companies in all sectors] If Yes, in addition to the sub-requirements that already apply, the company meets the following criteria. 
a) The company meets HR2.1, 2.3, and 2.4. 
b) The company considers the potential impact (see Intent) in the human rights saliency assessment (HR2.1).

[Small companies in all sectors] If Yes, in addition to the sub-requirements that already apply,
a) The company meets PSG4.2.
b) The company selects “not applicable” for PSG4.1 because PSG4.2 replaces it.

requirements.title: The company establishes a public purpose to make a meaningful positive impact.

subRequirements.title: The company establishes a public purpose to make a meaningful positive impact.

criteria.text:
The company establishes a purpose statement which:
a) sets out the specifc positive and meaningful impact the company intends to make on society or the environment, or both
b) has business relevance and is integrated into its strategy
c) is publicly available on the company’s webpage
d) is approved by the company’s highest governing body.

requirements.title: The company considers its impacts on stakeholders in decision-making.

subRequirements.title: The company has a mechanism to consider or involve its stakeholders and represent their interests in decision-making.

criteria.text: The company identifes and prioritizes its stakeholders and maps its stakeholders listed in 2.1.3. .
The company engages with its stakeholders and considers their interests in decision-making.

The following stakeholders are represented with one or more engagement mechanisms.
a) Workers of the company or its subsidiaries
b) Suppliers
c) Customers
d) Investors
e) The community where offces or facilities of the company, its subsidiaries, its suppliers, or its investments are located
f) The local or global environment

requirements.title: The company has adequate procedures to address stakeholder grievances.

subRequirements.title: The company has a publicly accessible grievance procedure allowing stakeholders to safely raise grievances and seek resolutions

criteria.text: The company publishes a grievance form on its webpage or has another easily accessible way for stakeholders to raise a grievance.

The grievance procedure explains:
a) grounds for accepting a grievance
b) grievance process steps and targeted deadlines for managing a grievance
c) how a resolution is facilitated
The company describes the processes and controls in place to protect stakeholders who raise grievances from any form of retaliation.

The company responds to stakeholder grievances by either:
a) regularly communicating each step in the resolution process and its outcome to the complainant, and confrming when the grievance hasbeen resolved
b) explaining why it did not accept the issue as a grievance.

subRequirements.title: The company tracks grievances and assigns accountability for resolving them.

criteria.text: The company monitors and tracks grievances and prepares annual summaries of the status and subject of any grievances.
The company has an employee with well-defned responsibilities for managing grievances

The company demonstrates the effectiveness of the grievance procedure by either:
a) recording evidence that a grievance has been resolved and closed
b) demonstrating that they have the appropriate grievance procedure in place (inclusive of tracking), where a company has had no grievancesfled

requirements.title: The company engages in responsible marketing and public relations.

subRequirements.title: The company has principles for responsible marketing and public relations practices.

criteria.text:
The principles include the following specifc references to the company’s marketing and public relations practices for environmental andsocial claims.
a) It makes precise, verifable, and substantiated claims based on reliable or scientifc data.
b) It is truthful, transparent, and accountable about the social and environmental impacts of the company's operations, both positive andnegative.
c) It follows ethical guidelines when using sensitive marketing and public relations channels and practices.
The principles are communicated to company workers and available for them to access.

The company documents the following principles governing its marketing and public relations practices related to environmental and socialclaims.
a) The company makes precise, verifable, and substantiated claims based on reliable or scientifc data.
b) The company is truthful, transparent, and accountable about the social and environmental impacts of the company's operations, bothpositive and negative.
c) The company follows ethical guidelines when using sensitive marketing and public relations channels and practices
The principles are communicated to company workers and available for them to access.

requirements.title: The company’s social and environmental impact and stakeholder considerations are monitored by the highest governing body and integrated throughout the company.

subRequirements.title: The highest governing body monitors the company's purpose, social and environmental impact, and stakeholder considerations

criteria.text:
At least once every 12 months, the highest governing body reviews the company’s:
a) progress on advancing its public purpose as defned under PSG1.1
b) social and environmental performance
c) stakeholder governance implementation

requirements.title: The company sets clear expectations of employees.

subRequirements.title: The company provides all employees a signed employment contract or offer letter.

criteria.text:
All employees have an employment contract or offer letter meeting the following criteria.
a) It is written in a language the employee understands.
b) It is signed by a company representative and the employee.
c) It includes:
i) the name of the companyi
i) the names of both signing partiesii
i) the nature and place of the worki
v) working hours
v) the base wagev
i) any extra wage componentsvi
i) the work start datevii
i) the duration of the workix) conditions for termination.
If an employee is already working without a written contract or offer letter, the company provides a letter that meets the criteria above
All employees receive a copy of their employment contract or offer letter from the company.

subRequirements.title: The company has equal cancellation periods when using variable schedules.

criteria.text:
If the company uses variable schedules, it has a policy that states the following.
a) The specifc cancellation deadline that applies equally to both the company and employee.
b) That the company will pay the employee in full when cancelling their work after the deadline for reasons within the company’s control.
c) Whether the company will pay the employee, and how much, when canceling their work after the deadline for reasons outside the company’scontrol.
The company makes the policy available to all employees that work variable schedules.

requirements.title: The company implements fair wage practices.

subRequirements.title: The company has a policy of not requesting wage histories from job applicants.

criteria.text:
The company has a policy or procedure that states it does not ask job applicants to provide:
a) their wage histories
b) their preferred wage (unless the company frst shares a wage scale).

subRequirements.title: The company tells workers how it sets their wage and what benefits they are entitled to.

criteria.text:
The company tells workers about:
a) all wage components relevant to them
b) all benefts they are entitled to
c) the mechanisms it uses for setting and reviewing wages and benefts

All employees regularly receive payslips or equivalent containing clear information about, at minimum, their:
a) base wage
b) extra wage components
c) deductions
Payslips are written in a language the employee understands.

requirements.title: The company considers feedback from workers on decisions that affect them.

subRequirements.title: The company considers feedback from workers on decisions that affect them.

criteria.text: The company seeks, considers, and addresses worker feedback on decisions that affect them.
The company seeks feedback from the workers affected by a decision, or their representative.
The company communicates its decision and how it considered feedback back to the relevant workers, or their representative.

requirements.title: The company measures workplace culture and takes action to improve it.

subRequirements.title: The company measures workplace culture regularly.

criteria.text: The measurement focuses on outcomes for workers.

The measurement includes at least two of the following themes.
a) Satisfaction
b) Wellbeing
c) Belonging
d) Feeling engaged
e) Being engaged
f) Psychological safety
The company states in its communications about the measurement that participation is optional.

The company completes the measurement:
a) in the twelve months before Year 0
b) in each subsequent year
The measurement is done annually.

If the company has 50 workers or more (based on headcoun
t) then:a) The measurement is both qualitative and quantitative.b) The measurement is anonymous by default. Where anonymity cannot be ensured, the company informs workers.

requirements.title: The company collects data to inform its JEDI actions.

subRequirements.title: The company facilitates a discussion or survey about JEDI principles in the workplace.

criteria.text:
The company has facilitated at least one discussion or survey about JEDI principles in the workplace:
a) in the twelve months before Year 0
b) in each subsequent year.
The company states in its communications about the discussion or survey that participation is optional.

If the company chooses to facilitate a discussion:
a) it is at least one hour long
b) the company records notes
The company collects feedback from participants about their experience of the discussion or survey.
If the company uses a survey, workers can choose to participate anonymously.

If the company has more than 10 and fewer than 50 workers (based on headcoun
t), it has facilitated at least one discussion or surveyabout JEDI principles in the workplace:a) in the twelve months before Year 0b) in each subsequent year

If the company chooses to facilitate a discussion:
a) it is at least one hour long
b) the company records notes.

If the company has 50 workers or more (based on headcoun
t) it:a) collects data on gender identity or sex at birth for at least fve worker-related measurements.b) disaggregates data to report internally on its chosen worker-related measurements.
Workers provide their data and participate voluntarily, and can choose to remain anonymous

requirements.title: The company chooses and implements JEDI actions

subRequirements.title: The company chooses its JEDI actions using data and stakeholder feedback, records them in a plan, and implements them.

criteria.text:
The company chooses and implements:
a) two JEDI actions before Year 0
b) four JEDI actions for Years 3 and 5

The company chooses at minimum one option from each set across Years 0, 3, and 5.
a) Foundation (JEDI2.a-e)
b) Within the Workplace (JEDI2.f-l)
c) Beyond the Workplace (JEDI2.m-s)
The company considers stakeholder feedback and data (from JEDI1) when choosing its actions
The company records its actions and status updates in a plan.
The plan was updated and shared with relevant stakeholders in the last twelve months.

The company’s plan:
a) contains deadlines
b) allocates resources
c) assigns responsibilities to specifc roles
The plan, including status updates, is available for workers to review at any time

subRequirements.title: The company commits publicly to JEDI principles. [Foundation]

criteria.text:
The company develops a JEDI commitment statement that:
a) is public
b) is approved by the executive team or highest governing body
c) applies to the company's policies and practices across operations, customers, and community
The company assigns accountability for the JEDI commitment to the executive team or highest governing body.

subRequirements.title: The company improves JEDI knowledge and capacity among leaders. [Foundation]

criteria.text: The company carries out training or a workshop on JEDI-related topics. At minimum, the training or workshop amounts to one full day perparticipant within a one-year period.

The company improves the JEDI knowledge or capacity of at least two of the following groups.
a) The highest governing body
b) The executive team
c) Human resources
d) Training & development
e) Managers

subRequirements.title: The company reviews and updates existing policies using JEDI principles. [Foundation]

criteria.text:
The company reviews at least fve policies that affect people using:
a) data from JEDI1
b) stakeholder feedback
c) its JEDI commitment statement, if applicable (JEDI2.
a)
d) its improved in-house knowledge or capacity, if applicable (JEDI2.
b)

The review looks at:
a) terminology used in the policies
b) impacts the policies have on people
c) relationships to JEDI principles
Following its review, the company updates the policies if needed.

subRequirements.title: The company’s highest governing body and executive team reflect the diversity of its community. [Foundation]

criteria.text: The company chooses three social identities using stakeholder feedback and the demographics of its community.
The company’s highest governing body and executive team refect the diversity of its community across its three chosen social identities.
The company calculates the ratios at any point in the last twelve months.

subRequirements.title: The company carries out an equity audit. [Foundation]

criteria.text: The company gets a third party with relevant expertise to carry out an equity audit.
The audit produces a report with a written summary of the audit methodology.
The equity audit includes feedback from relevant social identity groups.

The scope of the equity audit includes, at minimum, the company’s:
a) workers
b) internal and external communication
c) products and services.
The company publicly shares a summary of the audit results.
Audit participants can choose to remain anonymous.

subRequirements.title: The company supports at least two employee resource or affinity groups. [Within the Workplace]

criteria.text: The company supports at least two employee resource or affnity groups. Each group is associated with a different social identity.
The company chooses the social identities using worker feedback. '
Participation in the groups is optional for workers.
The company supports the groups.

subRequirements.title: The company implements inclusive hiring practices. [Within the Workplace]

criteria.text:
The company implements all of the following inclusive hiring practices.
a) It includes a JEDI commitment statement in all job postings, aligned with the statement from JEDI2.a (if complete
d).
b) It establishes a policy of not asking for credit checks or criminal records during the application process — unless required by law, or anindustry association or regulator.
c) It takes measures to reduce biases or their impacts in hiring processes.
d) It analyzes its job description language and requirements to ensure they are inclusive and equitable.

subRequirements.title: The company provides sponsorship and mentorship opportunities to workers. [Within the Workplace]

criteria.text: The company provides sponsorship or mentorship opportunities to all employees.
The company records the formal nature of the sponsorship or mentorship program in a procedure or policy document.

The sponsorships or mentorships:
a) are free for workers
b) last six months at minimum.
The company gives participants time during standard working hours to participate.
The company tracks participation of two underrepresented groups.
The company achieves representative participation of at least two underrepresented groups.

subRequirements.title: The company develops and implements an inclusive language guide for internal communications. [Within the Workplace]

criteria.text: The company develops an inclusive language guide for internal communications.
The guide lists terms that should and should not be used.
One guide exists for each internal communication language.
The company shares the guide with all workers who produce internal communications.

subRequirements.title: The company increases its proportion of workers from underrepresented groups to reflect the diversity of its community. [Within

criteria.text: The company increases the proportion of workers from at least two underrepresented groups to refect the diversity of its community.
The company calculates the ratios at any point in the last twelve months.

subRequirements.title: The company provides additional types of paid leave beyond legal minimums. [Within the Workplace]

criteria.text:
The company provides employees at least three of the following types of paid leave.
a) Unlimited short-term sick leave
b) Gender affrmation leave
c) Personal leave
d) Religious or cultural leave chosen by workers individually
e) Parental leave (at least 18 weeks)
f) Adoption leave
All leave types are fully paid.
All employees are entitled to the additional types of leave.
The company uses employee feedback to determine the number of days for each leave type.

The company records the chosen types of leave in a policy document or documents that are:
a) shared with all employees
b) available to read at all times.

subRequirements.title: The company’s internal communication tools meet accessibility standards. [Within the Workplace]

criteria.text: The company assesses the accessibility of its digital internal communication tools.

The assessment:
a) confrms the tools meet the AA or AAA criteria of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG)
b) is carried out by an internal or external specialist
c) includes manual testing
d) includes feedback from people with disabilities.

subRequirements.title: The company’s website meets accessibility standards. [Beyond the Workplace]

criteria.text: The company assesses the accessibility of its public-facing website.

The assessment:
a) confrms the website meets the AA or AAA criteria of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG)
b) is carried out by an internal or external specialist
c) includes manual testing
d) includes feedback from people with disabilities

subRequirements.title: The company communicates its JEDI action plan and progress publicly. [Beyond the Workplace]

criteria.text: The company communicates its JEDI action plan and progress publicly, once per year at minimum.

subRequirements.title: The company promotes diversity among its local suppliers. [Beyond the Workplace]

criteria.text:
The company implements all of the following actions.
a) It tracks diversity of ownership among its local suppliers.
b) It establishes a policy to give preferences to local suppliers owned by persons from underrepresented groups.
c) It sets targets to purchase a percentage of goods and services from local suppliers owned by persons from underrepresented groups

subRequirements.title: The company develops and implements an inclusive communications and ethical content guide for external communications.

criteria.text:
The company develops a communications and ethical content guide that:
a) lists terms that should and should not be used for each external communication language
b) describes how to gather, manage, and use content ethically
c) sets expectations for representing social identities
d) is shared with all workers who produce external communications
If the company uses artifcial intelligence for creative content generation, it includes its use in the guide.

subRequirements.title: The company assesses how inclusive a product or service is. [Beyond the Workplace]

criteria.text: The company uses stakeholder feedback to assess a product or service for inclusivity.

The assessment highlights:
a) which specifc social identity groups may experience barriers when accessing the product or service
b) what those barriers are.

subRequirements.title: The company redesigns a product or service to be more inclusive. [Beyond the Workplace]

criteria.text: The company uses stakeholder feedback to redesign one of its products or services to be more inclusive.
The company redesigns the original product or service, rather than designing a segregation solution.
The company offers the redesigned product or service to customers or announces it publicly.

subRequirements.title: The company takes part in at least one collective action to advance JEDI principles. [Beyond the Workplace]

criteria.text: The company engages in at least one collective action initiative at the policy, industry, or business community level to advance JEDIprinciples

The initiative has a clear, shared purpose and goal, to:
a) achieve systems change or transformation
b) collaboratively deliver specifc, measurable impacts.
The company makes a clear contribution to delivering the initiative

requirements.title: The company commits publicly to respecting human rights.

subRequirements.title: The company commits publicly to respecting human rights.

criteria.text:
The company commits publicly to respect human rights and to each of the following:
a) UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights
b) The International Bill of Rights or the rights under the Universal Declaration of Human Rights
c) The International Labour Organization’s (ILO) Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work

requirements.title: The company prevents, mitigates, and remediates actual and potential negative human rights impacts.

subRequirements.title: The company assesses the potential negative human rights impacts related to potential organizational clients and projects, andtakes necessary mitigation actions.

criteria.text: The company has a process in place to assess the potential negative human rights impacts of working with potential organizational clients and projects.
The process sets out mitigation actions.

The company records how it assessed the potential negative human rights impacts of its three most material potential clients or projectseach year, and the outcomes of the process.
a) in the last fscal year before Year 0
b) annually in each subsequent year.

For Years 3 and 5, the company:
a) records its mitigation action, if its assessments identifed any potential or actual negative impacts
b) records the effectiveness of its mitigation actions.

subRequirements.title: The company assesses the potential negative human rights impacts of investments, and takes necessary mitigation actions.

criteria.text: The company has a process in place to assess the potential negative human rights impacts of potential investments.
The process sets out mitigation actions.

The company records how it assessed the potential negative human rights impacts of its three most material potential investments eachyear, and the outcomes of the process
a) in the last fscal year before Year 0
b) annually in each subsequent year.

For Years 3 and 5, the company:
a) records its mitigation action, if its assessments identifed any potential or actual negative impacts
b) records the effectiveness of its mitigation actions.
The company has a process in place to assess the potential negative human rights impacts of working with potential organizational clientsand projects.
The process sets out mitigation actions.

The company records how it assessed the potential negative human rights impacts of its three most material potential clients or projectseach year, and the outcomes of the process.
a) in the last fscal year before Year 0
b) annually in each subsequent year.

For Years 3 and 5, the company:
a) records its mitigation action, if its assessments identifed any potential or actual negative impacts
b) records the effectiveness of its mitigation actions.

subRequirements.title: The company carries out a Human Rights Impact Assessment.

criteria.text: The company has a process in place to assess the potential negative human rights impacts of potential investments.
The process sets out mitigation actions.

The company records how it assessed the potential negative human rights impacts of its three most material potential investments eachyear, and the outcomes of the process
a) in the last fscal year before Year 0
b) annually in each subsequent year.

For Years 3 and 5, the company:
a) records its mitigation action, if its assessments identifed any potential or actual negative impacts
b) records the effectiveness of its mitigation actions.

requirements.title: The company works with suppliers to achieve its human rights objectives.

subRequirements.title: The company considers actual and potential human rights impacts in its procurement decisions.

criteria.text:
The company has considered the actual and potential human rights impacts of the three most material procurement decisions
a) in the last fscal year or twelve months before Year 0
b) in each subsequent year.

requirements.title: The company is committed to contribute to help keep global warming below 1.5 °C.

subRequirements.title: The company has a publicly available climate action plan.

criteria.text: The company publishes its climate action plan on its webpage or has another way for stakeholders to easily access it.

The company’s action plan:
a) commits to supporting the global ambition to limit global warming to 1.5°C
b) includes specifc, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (SMART) targets for performance and impact
c) specifes how the company will allocate human, technical, and material resources for implementation
d) outlines how the company will engage and work with stakeholders
e) is approved by the highest governing body.
The company updates its action plan every three years.

requirements.title: The company knows its actual and potential impacts on the environment.

subRequirements.title: The company monitors the animal welfare conditions in its operations.

criteria.text:
The company defines indicators to monitor animal welfare conditions. The indicators in its monitoring process relate to how the animalsare:
a) raised
b) transported
c) slaughtered.
The company monitors the fve freedoms of animal welfare.

The company creates an annual aggregate summary of animal welfare conditions:
a) in the fscal year before Year 0
b) in each subsequent year.
The company meets any applicable laws regarding animal welfare (both general and species-specifc).

subRequirements.title: The company assesses the potential negative environmental impacts related to potential organizational clients and projects,and takes necessary mitigation actions.

criteria.text: The company has a process in place to assess the potential negative environmental impacts of working with potential organizational clientsand projects.
The process sets out mitigation actions.

The company records how it assessed the potential negative environmental impacts of its three most material potential clients, and theoutcomes of the process:
a) in the fscal year before Year 0
b) annually in each subsequent year.

For Years 3 and 5 the company:
a) records the mitigation action it took, if its assessments identifed any potential or actual negative impacts
b) records the effectiveness of its mitigation actions

subRequirements.title: The company assesses the potential negative environmental impacts of investments, and takes necessary mitigation actions.

criteria.text: The company has a process in place to assess the potential negative environmental impacts of potential investments.
The process sets out mitigation actions.

The company records how it assessed the potential negative environmental impacts of its three most material potential clients, and theoutcomes of the process:
a) in the fscal year before Year 0
b) annually in each subsequent year

For Years 3 and 5, the company:
a) records the mitigation action it took, if its assessments identifed any potential or actual negative impacts
b) records the effectiveness of its mitigation actions

requirements.title: The company has a strategy to address its actual and potential negative environmental impacts, and to support staying within ecological thresholds.

subRequirements.title: The company assesses the potential negative environmental impacts related to potential organizational clients and projects,and takes necessary mitigation actions.

criteria.text: The company has a process in place to assess the potential negative environmental impacts of working with potential organizational clientsand projects.
The process sets out mitigation actions.

The company records how it assessed the potential negative environmental impacts of its three most material potential clients, and theoutcomes of the process:
a) in the fscal year before Year 0
b) annually in each subsequent year.

For Years 3 and 5 the company:
a) records the mitigation action it took, if its assessments identifed any potential or actual negative impacts
b) records the effectiveness of its mitigation actions

subRequirements.title: The company assesses the potential negative environmental impacts of investments, and takes necessary mitigation actions.

criteria.text: The company has a process in place to assess the potential negative environmental impacts of potential investments.
The process sets out mitigation actions.

The company records how it assessed the potential negative environmental impacts of its three most material potential investments, andthe outcomes of the process:
a) in the fscal year before Year 0
b) annually in each subsequent year.

For Years 3 and 5, the company:
a) records the mitigation action it took, if its assessments identifed any potential or actual negative impacts
b) records the effectiveness of its mitigation actions

requirements.title: The company works with suppliers to achieve its environmental objectives.

subRequirements.title: The company considers actual and potential environmental impacts in its procurement decisions.

criteria.text:
The company has considered the actual and potential environmental impacts for the three most material procurement decisions:
a) in the fscal year or twelve months before Year 0
b) in each subsequent year.

requirements.title: The company takes a responsible and transparent approach to lobbying.

subRequirements.title: The company has a public policy on responsible lobbying.

criteria.text: If the company is not engaged in lobbying, then it meets this sub-requirement by declaring this publicly

The company’s lobbying policy states its approach to responsible lobbying, including:
a) a statement that the company will lobby only to contribute to a positive impact on society or the environment
b) a statement that its lobbying approach is based on either reliable or scientifc data (or both)
c) its approach to fnancial and in-kind political contributions
d) its approach to anti-corruption and bribery
e) its approach to responsible lobbying with intermediary organizations, including controls that ensure consistency with the lobbying policy
f) which governance body within the company will formally review and approve the policy, and how frequently.

The company’s lobbying policy states its governance, control, and risk management practices, including:
a) which governance body or executive-level position within the company is accountable for enforcing the policy
b) how the policy is embedded within the company, including how the company puts it into practice
c) how the company identifes, manages, and monitors risks of non-compliance
d) how the company evaluates compliance with the governance and control framework
e) how stakeholders can raise concerns about the company’s business conduct and lobbying practices, including reference to the company’sgrievance procedure [link to PSG3].

The company’s lobbying policy is:
a) approved by the highest governing body
b) published on the company’s webpage and accessible to all stakeholders

criteria.text:
The company takes part in collective action from the fve options in this Impact Topic.
a) GACA2.1a The company mentors others in its industry, profession, or value chain to advance their social or environmental impacts.
b) GACA2.1b The company contributes to external research to advance social or environmental impacts.
c) GACA2.1c The company collaborates with multiple stakeholders to advance social or environmental impacts.
d) GACA2.1d The company promotes public policy to advance social or environmental impacts.
e) GACA2.1e The company uses thought leadership to drive systemic change towards an equitable, inclusive, and regenerative economy.

The company takes part in at least:
a) one collective action before Year 0
b) two of the fve collective action options for Years 3 and 5.
